# Inherited provider data reads fine but enumerates as {}

## Context

neomjs/neo-agent-institution#243 moves the cockpit's `goldenPathEnvelope` leaf up to the Viewport provider, so that a sibling keeper view can bind it. After that move, the cockpit's Route graph pane draws nothing. Its currency line, which is read through `get`, is correct. The canvas is empty because `GraphCanvas.pushEnvelope` hands the canvas worker `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(envelope))`, and in the cockpit's scope that serializes to `{}`.

Bisected: both Route graph visual arms pass at Institution `adad639f8e`. They fail with the leaf move alone, including with the new Observatory item removed entirely.

The Brain has hit the same gap twice and documented it at the use site instead of fixing it (neomjs/neo-agent-brain, dev `60f911e`):
- `ai/services/knowledge-base/SearchService.mjs`: `{...aiConfig.openAiCompatible}` "was measurably `{}`". The spread dropped `host`, which left the chat provider on Chroma's port.
- `ai/services/memory-core/CoalescingEngineService.mjs`: `{...wakeDispatch}` "is measurably `{}`", and the file carries a standing "never add a rest element" rule.

## The Problem

Measured on neo dev `f1302fb7d5` with a throwaway unit probe. The parent provider holds `{user: {name: 'Parent', role: 'admin'}}`, the child provider holds `{prefix: 'User:'}`, and `data` is the child's `getHierarchyData()`:

| read in the child scope | result |
|---|---|
| `data.user.name` | `'Parent'` |
| `JSON.stringify(data.user)` | `{}` |
| `Object.keys(data.user)` | `[]` |
| `{...data.user}` | `{}` |
| `Object.keys(data)` | `['prefix']` |

In the parent scope, `JSON.stringify(data.user)` is the full object.

A named read and an enumeration of the same proxy disagree, and nothing warns or throws. The first symptom appears downstream: an empty canvas, a request sent to the wrong port, or a validation error naming a leaf the caller can plainly see is set.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/state/createHierarchicalDataProxy.mjs` documents the proxy as "the merged, hierarchical data from a `state.Provider` chain". `component/Abstract#beforeGetData` documents `data` as "a merged parent state providers data map".
- The proxy's `get` and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps resolve through `Provider#getOwnerOfDataProperty` → `#findDataOwner`, which walks the parent chain. `Provider#hasNestedDataStartingWith` walks it too.
- The `ownKeys` trap calls `Provider#getTopLevelDataKeys(path)` (`src/state/Provider.mjs`). That method iterates only `this.#dataConfigs` and reads only this provider's `#dataKeyVersion`. It is the one trap that stops at the closest provider.

## The Fix

`getTopLevelDataKeys(path)` collects the top-level keys under `path` from every provider on the chain, closest first, into one Set. A key that the child declares therefore appears once, and its value still resolves to the child through `get`. Every visited provider's `#dataKeyVersion` is read, so an enumeration re-runs when any provider on the chain gains a key. This is the same walk `#findDataOwner` already makes (`parent.#findDataOwner(...)`). No proxy trap changes.

Unit arms go in `test/playwright/unit/state/ProviderNestedDataConfigs.spec.mjs`, using real `Neo.state.Provider` instances on parent and child components:
- An inherited object enumerates, and round-trips through JSON, in the child scope.
- Keys under one path merge across the chain (child `user.nickname` + parent `user.name`).
- A key declared on both levels appears once and reads the child's value.
- An effect that enumerates the child scope re-runs when the parent gains a key.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enumeration of a hierarchical data proxy (`Object.keys`, spread, rest, `JSON.stringify`, `for…in`) | `createHierarchicalDataProxy` JSDoc ("the merged, hierarchical data"); `Abstract#beforeGetData` JSDoc | Enumerates the keys `get` resolves: the union over the provider chain, closest provider first | A key absent on every provider stays absent | `Provider#getTopLevelDataKeys` JSDoc | The unit arms above |

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a child provider's scope, an object inherited from a parent provider enumerates its keys, and `JSON.stringify` / spread / `Object.keys` produce what the parent scope produces.
- [ ] Keys under one path merge across the chain. A key declared on both levels appears once and reads the closest provider's value.
- [ ] An effect that enumerates a child scope re-runs when a parent provider gains a key under the enumerated path.
- [ ] The `test/playwright/unit/state/` suite stays green.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The Route graph visual arms of neomjs/neo-agent-institution#243 pass once the Institution engine pin includes this fix.

## Out of Scope

- The Brain's two use-site workarounds keep working after this lands, because named reads are unchanged. Their "measurably `{}`" explanations go stale once the Brain's engine pin includes the fix; updating them belongs to the Brain.
- Leaf values that are themselves objects (Records, non-drilled objects) are unchanged.
